payload.summary: Reviewed three budget-tracking amendments against the actual codebase implementation. The oxygen guard omission is a genuine gap that should be addressed given the infrastructure already exists. The compile-time gating and per-pool test granularity concerns are valid observations but not actionable defects.

votes.rationale: Confirmed by code inspection: enforce_tracked_tick_budget_guard (engine.rs:524-548) checks nitrogen and carbon residuals but completely ignores the oxygen field that BudgetDelta already carries. The dissolved_oxygen system is already instrumented with budget tracking (step_dissolved_oxygen_with_budget returns a BudgetDelta with oxygen ElementBudget), and reaeration is an open-system atmospheric exchange analogous to the DIC chemistry shortcut that carbon_guard_delta_mg already subtracts via chemistry_external_carbon_flux_mg. The pattern for adding an oxygen guard is clear: compute oxygen residual = net_delta.oxygen.net_mg() minus the dissolved_oxygen stage's known reaeration flux, then check against a tolerance. The acceptance criteria explicitly say 'Track oxygen demand in the same framework where feasible' — the framework is already in place, only the guard check is missing. At minimum, the omission should be documented with a comment explaining why oxygen is excluded from the guard. Accepting this amendment.

The acceptance criteria specify 'compiles out OR is zero-cost when not in use' — this is a disjunction, and the implementation satisfies the second clause. When budget_ledger is None: BudgetSnapshot::from_state is never called (gated by if tick.is_some() checks in maybe_record_stage), no allocations occur, and no budget math runs. The unconditionally compiled types (BudgetLedger, BudgetSnapshot, ElementBudget, helper functions) are tiny structs and pure functions that the linker can strip as dead code in release builds when unused. The test test_budget_ledger_zero_cost_when_disabled correctly validates the meaningful runtime claim. Adding a cargo feature flag would increase build matrix complexity (especially for CI and downstream consumers) with no practical benefit. The amendment itself concedes this is 'a defensible design choice.' Rejecting.

The concern about aggregate-based testing is theoretically valid but already mitigated by the structural coverage test test_budget_component_labels_cover_all_element_bearing_fields (budget_tracking.rs:337-372), which serializes TankState to JSON, discovers all element-bearing fields by naming convention, and asserts exact set equality with the component labels returned by nitrogen_budget_components(). If any microbe pool were omitted from the helper, this structural test would fail because the field path would be discovered but not appear in the component label set. Adding per-pool assertions to the sum test would make it more brittle to refactoring (any change to pool count or conversion factors requires updating the test) without adding meaningful safety beyond the structural test. The linearity of the conversions means the aggregate test correctly validates the total regardless of individual pool ordering. Rejecting.
